pr_body:
Add pager functionality to the following commands:
- gist list
- pr checks
- release list
- run list
- run view
- secret list
- workflow list
- workflow view

Additionally, normalize error handling when starting the pager has failed: only print a non-fatal notice to stderr instead of aborting the whole command.

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5102

issue_context.title: Show PR checks summary after checks statuses
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

The command `gh pr checks <PR>` shows the summary before showing the checks statuses. When the terminal window is small, or if there are many checks to display, this can involve scrolling up to see the summary:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1149246/151108518-0fc6fa0b-62ff-4cc6-92cf-c0487541fa00.mov

### Proposed solution

Show the summary after the checks statuses

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1149246/151108537-312d9e27-1802-448e-9fb1-6a4cb5131c30.mov

I also think it would be clearer to add an additional space between the checks and the summary in this implementation.

### Additional context

I have this implemented on a fork and would be happy to open a PR if this is a helpful approach.
comments:
Hi, thank you for pointing this out!

Typically, issues with small terminals and having control over the scrollback are solved by configuring your PAGER (alternatively, by `gh config set pager`). However, the bug here is that the `pr checks` command does not pipe its output through PAGER if configured. I will open a PR to resolve this.

With PAGER configured and this issue fixed, you will no longer need to scroll back to view the summary. This way we can keep the output format intact.

review_comments: How does a pager interpret/interact with the progress indicator? I think the pager was started in this command explicitly after the progress indicator, but I don't actually know if they conflict.

Good question! In my testing it's fine if the progress indicator continues to spin even after the pager has started, but ideally it should never be started after the first output has been written to stdout.
Is there a reason to explicitly pass in `ref` here? Seems like we are still passing in `opts`.

That's a valid observation, but I felt it was much more clear for the signature of the method to receive the ref as argument rather than inferring it from `opts`. Furthermore, I feel like having too many methods having `opts` as a receiver or argument is an antipattern because it dis-incentivizes the method from having a very limited responsibility. This small refactoring was a step towards not passing `opts` as an argument in the future.
